Portal 2 is a flawless masterpiece of game design that seamlessly blends mind-bending physics puzzles with one of the greatest narrative experiences in gaming history. Armed with a device that opens interconnected portals, you navigate increasingly complex, physics-defying test chambers that reward creative spatial thinking and lateral logic. What truly elevates the game is its brilliant writing, dark humor, and unforgettable characters like the passive-aggressive GLaDOS and the hilariously incompetent Wheatley, all brought to life by impeccable voice acting. Complete with a stellar standalone cooperative campaign that requires perfect communication between two players, it is a perfectly paced, visually enduring, and intellectually stimulating triumph that every gamer should experience.

Bought 5 years ago to trial it, got 2.1 hours so I couldn’t refund.

Came back 5 years later with a friend to play co-op, got roasted by Glados MULTIPLE TIMES, ended up crushing friend in a non lethal maze somehow.

10/10!

Portal 2 is a flawless masterpiece of game design that seamlessly blends mind-bending physics puzzles with one of the greatest narrative experiences in gaming history. Armed with a device that opens interconnected portals, you navigate increasingly complex, physics-defying test chambers that reward creative spatial thinking and lateral logic. What truly elevates the game is its brilliant writing, dark humor, and unforgettable characters like the passive-aggressive GLaDOS and the hilariously incompetent Wheatley, all brought to life by impeccable voice acting. Complete with a stellar standalone cooperative campaign that requires perfect communication between two players, it is a perfectly paced, visually enduring, and intellectually stimulating triumph that every gamer should experience.

Fifteen years later, Portal 2 is still one of the finest puzzle games ever made.

Its greatest achievement isn't the story or the humor—it's the level design.

The entire game revolves around a single mechanic: the Portal Gun. No endless list of weapons, no constantly expanding skill trees, no unnecessary complexity. Yet Valve managed to build an entire game around one brilliant idea, and somehow kept introducing fresh puzzles from beginning to end.
The puzzles are genuinely challenging. Many of them left me staring at the room for minutes, testing one possibility after another. Sometimes it took dozens of attempts before everything finally clicked.

But that's exactly why solving them feels so satisfying.

The game never hands you the answer. It simply gives you the tools and trusts you to figure it out yourself.

I ended up playing almost the entire game in one sitting. It was so mentally demanding that I actually started getting a headache—but I couldn't stop. Every solved chamber immediately made me want to see what the next one had in store.

That's the mark of truly exceptional game design.

Fifteen years have passed, and countless puzzle games have come and gone.

Yet very few have managed to surpass what Portal 2 accomplished with nothing more than a portal gun and extraordinary level design.

Highly recommended.

If I'd played this game when I was five, I'd probably have won the Nobel Prize in Physics by now. XD

citations.review_text:
Single best video game ever made. Also a great starter for your significant other who isn't into gaming yet. Innovative mechanics, great story, appealing visual design and superb voice acting.

The co-op is worth the entry price alone.

Portal 2 is one of those once-in-a-generation sequels that is merely par for the course when it comes to Valve. While it doesn't beg for a third game in the same way its sister franchise Half-Life does, I think it would be a welcome addition to the 2020s as well as a wonderful opportunity to revisit Aperture Science in an official capacity once again. While the isolation of the facility is intentional, Cave Johnson, GLadOS and Wheatley make up a very colorful cast for the only voices you hear in the game!

The Co-op mode is something I've enjoyed with many different friends and family members, and is a clear format setter for the much more recent co-op exclusive games of this decade, integrating puzzles that require communication and timing with a partner.

I hope Cave Johnson's lab boys are tinkering on a future Portal concept, or they'll be missing out on a nice crisp $60 right in their pockets, with a minimal amount of science stuff put in them!

Direct upgrade from the original. More puzzles, more mechanics, more diverse environments, more achievements, fleshes out GLaDOS and Chell, introduces fantastic new characters, has an entirely fleshed out Co-Op mode with it's own story, etc. Truly the perfect puzzle game for everyone. Valve does not make a bad product.

10/10 Puzzle game with such a good story, fantastic follow up to the previous title, even better with the entire second campaign that is stricly 2 player cooperative. Definatley worth playing through both campaigns for the story and crazy mechanics.

citations.review_text: Perhaps the greatest game ever created. Beautiful design, fantastic storyline, and brilliant voice acting. The puzzles are incredible and fun, and each new mechanic is introduced in such a way that it never becomes overwhelming or overly difficult, yet maintains a challenging arc as the game progresses. Then add to it the workshop, and being able to create your own puzzles and publish them for others to play, and you have, in this old man's opinion, sheer perfection.

This is possibly the best sequel ever, if not the best game of all time. with community levels, there is never nothing new to do. so many people make really clever levels that there's always new content. not to mention the campaign, which is some of the best story lines ever.

One of the best puzzle games ever

Played so many community chambers that the game failed to find more

My favourite game of all time. And one of my proudest 100% achievements because I managed to beat it solo coop - Steam Deck + PC as setup. Not that you should tho. Get a friend and play the coop. It's simple 10/10.

Aside from the phenomenal coop the campaign is simply flawless. The story, voice acting, puzzles and mechanics. There is a good reason why this is one of the highest rated games of all time.

With constant community support you will find countless puzzles in the workshop. 
The only major recommendation I can give - before playing this play the first game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the puzzle mechanics as introducing new elements progressively without becoming overwhelming.

citations.review_text: Perhaps the greatest game ever created. Beautiful design, fantastic storyline, and brilliant voice acting. The puzzles are incredible and fun, and each new mechanic is introduced in such a way that it never becomes overwhelming or overly difficult, yet maintains a challenging arc as the game progresses. Then add to it the workshop, and being able to create your own puzzles and publish them for others to play, and you have, in this old man's opinion, sheer perfection.

About a couple months back, I wanted to revisit the Portal series as I've never really played it myself. So I bought both the first and second game. I could go on saying how good it is even though most of the reviews are overwhelmingly positive, but I'd like to also dedicate this review to also complimenting the detail and ambiance that comes with this game. When you boot up the game, you don't know where you are after the first one, waking up who knows how long after the conclusion prior, when you explore, everything is all dirty, rusty, worn out, etc. You hear the outside sure, and yet trapped doing test chambers that somehow can be solved even after so long. Some test chambers are taken from the original 19, but most of them are new and innovative. After playing for awhile, you see the test chambers slowly get fixed up, with each element being installed, each wall figuring out where to go, and of course with some music to go with it. I think this game is perfect, the humor, the ambiance, the music, everything was made with so much effort. And that's just the single player campaign, there's the level editor and the CO-OP mode too. I very much recommend.

Bruh, this is portal 2! if you aint played it yet, please do! its a great game, and expands and improves upon nearly everything from portal 1 (another game you should really play if you havent).
it takes place after portal 1 (or more simply, just "portal") and should be played after that.
the lighting is great, the puzzles are good, theres more variety in the themeing of each level, much more story and exposition about what really happened, and a very "mask off" sense of music design that the first game had to hold onto to not spoil the surprize. but with this game, its trying to kill you right from the jump, and has no reason to hold back on the spook factor of the music.
the new puzzle elements really add to the level design, and help blend the puzzleing sections with the acrobatic sections more neatly. like an eagle piloting a blimp.
its got a new multiplayer mode. and an ingame level editor for both single player AND multiplayer (i think, either that or theres a mod for it, i dont quite remember).

and just in general everything about this game was a breath of fresh air when it first came out. (such a shame then that until half life alyx released, this was their last major singleplayer game they released)

but still if YOU havent played it, i HIGHLY reccomend it. and bring a friend too! why not.
